handoff: Changes requested. F1 (blocking, AC7/B67): config set of a key that already holds a list or map (e.g. replacing notifiers whole, AC3) still re-renders the whole YAML doc, so padded inline comments on untouched lines change ('manual   # who' -> 'manual # who'). Scalars, new keys and unset splice correctly. F2 minor: agents.<name> seeded from built-in. F3 nit: no --user+--repo test. AC1-6, AC8 are met. The CLI test suite was still running at report time.

findings.title: Replacing an existing list (or any non-scalar value) re-renders the file and rewrites untouched lines
findings.detail:
withScalar returns null when the node is not a scalar or the new value is an object/list. withNewKey returns null because the key exists. So `text` falls back to rendered(doc). Repro (editConfigLayer, file repo) on `default_mode: manual   # who
notifiers:
  - adapter: os
` with key notifiers, set `[{adapter: os}, {adapter: os}]` gives `default_mode: manual # who` (padding lost) plus the new list: the untouched default_mode line differs. AC7: 'after `config set` only the changed line differs (comments and key order kept)'. B67: 'keep the file's comments and key order'. AC3 names list replacement (`notifiers '[{adapter: os}]'`) as a supported set. The same applies to a scalar replaced by a map or list, and to agents.<name> fields set into an existing block map (scalar fields are spliced; new fields go through withNewKey, so those are fine). The tests in config.test.ts only cover padded comments for scalars and new keys.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Splice an existing non-scalar value too: replace the lines of the pair's value (key range to the end of the value) with the stringified `key: value` block at the pair's indentation, keeping the meaning check. Add a red test: a padded-comment file, set an existing list, expect a diff limited to the list's lines.

findings.title: Seeding agents.<name> from the built-in agent ignores the other layer's agent
findings.detail:
setIn seeds a missing agents.<name> from DEFAULT_CONFIG.agents. When the user layer already redefines agents.claude (custom args), `config set agents.claude.model opus --repo` writes the built-in args into the repo file, and that repo entry then replaces the user's agent whole. This is a deliberate decision recorded in the handoff, so not blocking. Worth a line in the command's output or docs.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Seed from the resolved value below this layer (the built-in, or for repo the merged built-in+user), or mention the seeding in the set output.

findings.title: No test for --user and --repo together
findings.detail:
layerFile refuses `--user --repo` with a usage error. No test pins it.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: One integration case asserting exit 2 and the do_instead.
